payload.title: Diamond Buying Guide for Engagement Rings
payload.audience: Couples in their 30s, affluent, interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences beyond that, AUD 150k+ budget
payload.reader: A well-travelled couple in their mid 30s, one of whom is about to buy a diamond for a proposal (often planned abroad), who can afford a significant stone but do not want to be sold to, and who want to walk into any jeweller, at home or overseas, knowing which questions to ask, how to read and check a grading report, and what to do about natural versus lab-grown, ethics and carrying the stone through customs.
payload.goal: Click through to the destinations hub to start picturing where the proposal or wedding could happen (Wedded Concierge at /wonderland-concierge as secondary CTA).
payload.angle: Most diamond buying guides are written by retailers and end in their own product grid; this one has nothing to sell you in the stone itself, so it ranks the 4Cs by what actually changes how a diamond looks on the hand, shows how to check a GIA or IGI report number yourself before money changes hands, explains how natural and lab-grown stones are graded and disclosed differently, is honest about what the Kimberley Process does and does not cover, and adds the part retail guides skip: buying a diamond abroad or carrying one to a proposal or destination wedding (declarations, insurance cover overseas, keeping the report with the stone). It ends with a one-page shortlist checklist a couple can take into any appointment.
must_include: Cut: what it means for a round brilliant (graded) versus fancy shapes (no single cut grade on most reports), and why it drives sparkle more than any other C; source GIA
Colour: the D-to-Z scale in plain words, how setting metal affects perceived colour, where the eye stops noticing differences in general terms; source GIA
Clarity: the clarity scale, inclusions versus blemishes, the idea of 'eye-clean' and why it depends on size and shape; source GIA
Carat: weight not size, why two stones of the same carat can face up differently, and 'magic sizes' explained without any price figures; source GIA
Which C matters most: a clear editorial view (cut first for rounds, then balance colour and clarity against size), framed as guidance with the reasoning shown, not a rule

Shape: the main shapes (round, oval, cushion, emerald, pear, princess, radiant, marquise, Asscher) and how shape interacts with the 4Cs (e.g. bow-tie in elongated shapes, step cuts showing clarity); link the ring styles post for overall look

Grading reports: what a GIA or IGI report includes, laser inscription of the report number on the girdle, and how to check a report number on the lab's own online verification before buying; note that labs differ and a report is not an appraisal or valuation

Natural versus lab-grown: both are real diamond; how GIA and IGI grade and identify lab-grown stones, how reports and inscriptions disclose origin, and what Australian consumer law expects about clear disclosure (ACCC); no price or resale figures

Ethics and origin: what the Kimberley Process certifies (rough diamond trade between participating countries, conflict diamonds as it defines them) and its known limits (narrow definition, does not cover labour or environmental standards, chain-of-custody gaps); what questions to ask a jeweller about origin; source the KP itself and reputable reporting
Fluorescence: what it is, how reports describe it, when strong fluorescence can affect appearance and when it does not; source GIA

Buying or carrying a diamond abroad: declaring on return to Australia, GST and duty in general terms only with a [[VERIFY]] against Australian Border Force, keeping the grading report and receipt with the stone, carrying in hand luggage, checking that insurance covers travel and overseas, Smartraveller general safety advice; no figures unless sourced

A shortlist checklist (printable feel): shape, cut grade or proportions, colour and clarity range, carat range, report lab and number checked online, inscription matches, natural or lab-grown confirmed in writing, origin questions asked, fluorescence noted, return and resizing policy, insurance arranged before travel
FAQ (4 to 6 questions drawn from PAA once SEO research lands)

Internal links: /style-advice/engagement-ring-styles, /style-advice/engagement-ring-setting-for-active-lifestyle, /style-advice/celebrity-engagement-rings, /expert-advice/how-much-should-you-spend-on-an-engagement-ring (for any budget question), /destinations (primary CTA), /wonderland-concierge (secondary CTA), plus optionally /proposal/how-to-propose-a-step-by-step-guide-to-the-perfect-moment
Soft bridge to the destination proposal or wedding using only brand-facts.md claims
avoid: Any prices, price-per-carat figures, percentage premiums or 'spend X months' salary' style rules (link the ring budget article instead)
Naming or recommending jewellers, retailers or brands; GIA and IGI are named only as grading laboratories, and no lab is ranked with invented claims
Resale value or investment claims for natural or lab-grown diamonds
Calling lab-grown diamonds 'fake', 'simulants' or 'imitation', or implying natural is automatically more ethical
Claiming the Kimberley Process guarantees a diamond is 'ethical' or 'conflict-free' in a broad sense
Customs thresholds, duty rates or GST figures stated without an Australian Border Force source ([[VERIFY]] if used)
Invented statistics (e.g. share of buyers choosing lab-grown) unless sourced
Settings mechanics and style catalogue in depth (link the sister posts instead)
Gendered assumptions about who proposes or wears the ring; use 'your partner' or 'the wearer'
Business details not in brand-facts.md (fees, named Advisor, Wedded Privileges specifics are deferred)
Copying wording, structure or images from jewellers, labs' marketing or competitors, including Easy Weddings
Em dashes and US spelling (jewellery, colour, jeweller, travelling)
